cards.text: Jehu, the man just anointed king over Israel (2 Kings 9:6), has shot Joram king of Israel (2 Kings 9:24), and his men have shot Ahaziah king of Judah (2 Kings 9:27). Joram was the son of Ahab, an earlier king of Israel (1 Kings 16:29; 2 Kings 3:1), and Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria. So Jehu writes letters to the officials, the elders and the guardians of Ahab's sons.
Jehu's letter starts out like a checklist. Your master's sons, chariots, horses, a fortified city, weapons: check, check, check, CHECK, CHECK.

cards.question: With all those chariots and weapons in Samaria, what does Jehu's letter tell the officials to do?

answers.text: Crown the best son and fight for Ahab's house
Send the seventy sons away to Judah
Hand their chariots and horses to Jehu

cards.question: The officials in Samaria get ready to fight Jehu.
The officials are terrified. They reason that if ___ kings could not stand against Jehu, there's no way they can.

cards.text: So the palace administrator, the overseer of the city, the elders and the guardians send Jehu a message: "We are your servants, and we will do whatever you say." Chariots, horses, a whole fortified city, and they fold like a lawn chair.

cards.question: When the officials of Samaria send their answer back to Jehu, what do they promise they will NOT do?

cards.text: Then Jehu writes them a second letter: if you're on my side and you'll obey me, bring the heads of your master's sons to me at Jezreel by this time tomorrow. The seventy sons are being raised by the leading men of the city.

cards.question: When Jehu's second letter arrives, the leading men of Samaria do what Jehu says.

cards.text: This is a hard one to read, friend. They slaughter all seventy of the king's sons and send their heads to Jezreel in baskets, and Jehu orders them piled in two heaps at the entrance of the gate until morning.
The next morning, Jehu goes out, stands before all the people and tells them, "You are innocent."

cards.question: Standing before all the people, what does Jehu admit he did?

answers.text: Conspired against his master and killed him
Sent his men to burn down Samaria
Broke his promise to the elders

cards.text: Then Jehu asks about the heads at the gate: "But who killed all these?"

cards.question: Jehu tells the people that not a word the LORD has spoken against the house of Ahab will fail.
Jehu says the LORD has done what He promised against the house of Ahab. Through which servant of His did the LORD promise it?

cards.text: So Jehu kills everyone in Jezreel who remained of the house of Ahab, as well as all his great men, close friends and priests, leaving him without a single survivor.
Then Jehu sets out toward Samaria. At Beth-eked of the Shepherds, he meets some men, and he asks the question you never want to hear from a man like Jehu: "Who are you?"

cards.question: At Beth-eked, who do the men tell Jehu they are?

answers.text: Relatives of Ahaziah king of Judah
Servants of Hazael king of Aram
Prophets from the city of Bethel

cards.question: Ahaziah's relatives say they've come down to ___ the sons of the king and of the queen mother.

cards.text: Then Jehu orders, "Take them alive." His men do, then slaughter them at the well of Beth-eked, forty-two men in all, and he spares none of them.

Leaving there, Jehu finds Jehonadab son of Rechab coming to meet him, and Jehu greets him and asks, "Is your heart as true to mine as my heart is to yours?" Friend, after everything Jehu's done on this trip, that is NOT a casual hello.

cards.question: Jehonadab tells Jehu that his heart is true.
Once Jehonadab gives Jehu his hand, Jehu sends him on ahead to Samaria.
As Jehu helps Jehonadab into his chariot, what does Jehu invite Jehonadab to come and see?

cards.text: Jehonadab's riding in the chariot when Jehu comes to Samaria. There Jehu strikes down everyone belonging to Ahab who remained, until he has destroyed them, according to the word the LORD had spoken to Elijah.
That's all for this batch, friend. Jehu's chariot is still rolling, and his story keeps going.
